'''Sunetra Gupta''' (born 15 March 1965<ref name="Who's Who">{{Who's Who|id=U246715|title=Gupta, Prof. Sunetra}}</ref>) is an Indian-born British infectious disease epidemiologist and a professor of theoretical [[epidemiology]] at the [[Department of Zoology, University of Oxford]]. She has performed research on the transmission dynamics of various infectious diseases, including [[malaria]], [[influenza]] and [[COVID-19]], and has received the [[Zoological Society of London#Awards|Scientific Medal]] of the Zoological Society of London and the [[Rosalind Franklin Award]] of the Royal Society. She is a member of the scientific advisory board of Collateral Global, an organisation which examines the global impact of COVID-19 restrictions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ABOUT US |url=https://collateralglobal.org/about/ |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=Collateral Global |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Gupta is also a novelist and a recipient of the [[Sahitya Akademi Award]].

==Early life and education==
Gupta was born in [[Kolkata]], India, to Dhruba and Minati Gupta.<ref>{{Citation | title = Weekend Birthdays| newspaper = The Guardian| page = 51 | date = 15 March 2014}}</ref> She trained in biology, and was awarded a bachelor's degree from [[Princeton University]]. In 1992 she obtained her PhD from [[Imperial College London]] for a thesis on the transmission dynamics of infectious diseases.<ref name="guptaphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Sunetra|last=Gupta |title=Heterogeneity and the transmission dynamics of infectious diseases |publisher=Imperial College London |date=1992 |url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.309107|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.309107}}|author-link=Sunetra Gupta}}</ref>

==Career and research==
===Positions===
Gupta is a professor of theoretical [[epidemiology]] in the Department of Zoology at the [[University of Oxford]], where she leads a team of infectious disease epidemiologists. She has undertaken research on various infectious diseases,<ref name="LifeScientific"/> including [[malaria]], [[HIV]], [[influenza]], [[bacterial meningitis]] and [[COVID-19]]. She is a [[Fellow#In ancient universities|supernumerary fellow]] of [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-sunetra-gupta |title=Professor Sunetra Gupta: Supernumerary Fellow |website= College Life & People  |publisher=Merton College, Oxford |access-date=7 October 2020 }}</ref> She also sits on the European Advisory Board of [[Princeton University Press]].<ref>[http://press.princeton.edu/about_pup/european_advisory_board.html Princeton University Press, European Advisory Board] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608160559/http://press.princeton.edu/about_pup/european_advisory_board.html |date=2011-06-08 }}</ref>

In April 2021, she received a £90,000 donation from the [[Georg von Opel|Georg and Emily von Opel Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-13 |title=Covid-19 and the new merchants of doubt |url=https://blogs.bmj.com/bmj/2021/09/13/covid-19-and-the-new-merchants-of-doubt/ |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=The BMJ |language=en-US}}</ref> In May 2022 she joined a partnership with Blue Water Vaccines, Inc. to apply her research to the development of a universal flu vaccine.<ref>{{cite web |title=New boost to universal flu vaccine development |url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/article/new-boost-to-universal-flu-vaccine-development |publisher=[[Department of Biology, University of Oxford]] |access-date=17 August 2022}}</ref>

=== Awards ===
Gupta has been awarded the 2007 Scientific Medal by the [[Zoological Society of London]]<ref>{{cite web|title=ZSL Scientific Medal Winners|url=https://www.zsl.org/sites/default/files/media/2019-12/ZSL%20Scientific%20Medal%20Winners.pdf|access-date=11 October 2020|publisher=[[Zoological Society of London]]}}</ref> and the 2009 [[Royal Society]] [[Rosalind Franklin Award]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Surviving pandemics: a pathogen's perspective|url=https://royalsociety.org/science-events-and-lectures/2009/surviving-pandemics/|access-date=11 October 2020|publisher=[[Royal Society]]}}</ref> In July 2013, Gupta's portrait was on display during the prestigious [[Royal Society]]'s Summer Science Exhibition along with leading female scientist such as [[Madame Curie]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Indian woman scientist's portrait to be exhibited in Britain|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/nri/nri-achievers/Indian-woman-scientists-portrait-to-be-exhibited-in-Britain/articleshow/21216983.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130725040146/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-07-21/nri-achievers/40708277_1_indian-woman-scientist-image-problem-calcutta|archive-date=25 July 2013|work=[[The Times of India]]|url-status=live|access-date=1 September 2013}}</ref> She was elected a [[Royal Society of Literature|Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-11 |title=Gupta, Sunetra |url=https://rsliterature.org/fellows/gupta-sunetra/,%20https://rsliterature.org/fellows/gupta-sunetra/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== COVID-19 ===
{{further|Great Barrington Declaration}}
In March 2020, some modelling of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] by Gupta and colleagues was released to the media.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cookson |first=Clive |date=24 March 2020 |title=Coronavirus may have infected half of UK population — Oxford study |url=https://www.ft.com/content/5ff6469a-6dd8-11ea-89df-41bea055720b |work=Financial Times |location=London |access-date=11 January 2022}}</ref> Their model suggested that up to 68% of the UK population could already have been infected, suggesting broader immunity and a subsiding threat. The findings differed greatly from the work of other experts and quickly came under criticism.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Sayburn |first1= Anna|date=25 March 2020 |title=Covid-19: experts question analysis suggesting half UK population has been infected |url=https://www.bmj.com/content/368/bmj.m1216 |journal=The BMJ |volume=368 |issue= |article-number= m1216|doi=10.1136/bmj.m1216 |pmid= 32213506|s2cid= 214681140|access-date=11 January 2022|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In May that year, she told [[UnHerd]] that she believed "the epidemic has largely come and is on its way out in [the UK]. So, I think [the infection fatality rate] would be definitely less than one in a thousand, and probably closer to one in ten thousand."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DKh6kJ-RSMI&ab_channel=UnHerd|title=Professor Sunetra Gupta: the epidemic is on its way out|date=21 May 2020|publisher=YouTube|access-date=14 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Sayers |first=Freddie |date=21 May 2020 |title=Sunetra Gupta: Covid-19 is on the way out |url=https://unherd.com/2020/05/oxford-doubles-down-sunetra-gupta-interview/ |magazine=UnHerd |location=London |publisher= |access-date=11 January 2022}}</ref> A one in ten thousand infection fatality rate (IFR) was impossible for the spring of 2020 given the number of COVID deaths and the size of the UK population.<ref name="Lawson">{{cite news |last1=Lawson |first1=Dominic |title=Lockdown didn't need this dodgy dossier |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/lockdown-didnt-need-this-dodgy-dossier-0v3ktm0mv |access-date=27 October 2023 |date=27 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> Contemporaneous estimates of other experts for the IFR fell in a range much higher than this.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Estimates of the severity of coronavirus disease 2019: a model-based analysis|date=30 March 2020|publisher=The Lancet|pmid=32240634 |last1=Verity |first1=R. |last2=Okell |first2=L. C. |last3=Dorigatti |first3=I. |last4=Winskill |first4=P. |last5=Whittaker |first5=C. |last6=Imai |first6=N. |last7=Cuomo-Dannenburg |first7=G. |last8=Thompson |first8=H. |author9=Walker PGT |last10=Fu |first10=H. |last11=Dighe |first11=A. |last12=Griffin |first12=J. T. |last13=Baguelin |first13=M. |last14=Bhatia |first14=S. |last15=Boonyasiri |first15=A. |last16=Cori |first16=A. |last17=Cucunubá |first17=Z. |last18=Fitzjohn |first18=R. |last19=Gaythorpe |first19=K. |last20=Green |first20=W. |last21=Hamlet |first21=A. |last22=Hinsley |first22=W. |last23=Laydon |first23=D. |last24=Nedjati-Gilani |first24=G. |last25=Riley |first25=S. |last26=Van Elsland |first26=S. |last27=Volz |first27=E. |last28=Wang |first28=H. |last29=Wang |first29=Y. |last30=Xi |first30=X. |journal=The Lancet. Gupta has been a critic of [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdowns]] in the pandemic.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She was one of the three authors of the [[Great Barrington Declaration]] in 2020, which advocated lifting [[COVID-19]] restrictions on lower-risk groups to develop [[herd immunity]] through infection, while stating that vulnerable people should be protected from the virus.<ref name="MedPage2">{{Cite web |last=D'Ambrosio |first=Amanda |date=October 19, 2020 |title=Who Are the Scientists Behind the Great Barrington Declaration? |url=https://www.medpagetoday.com/infectiousdisease/covid19/89204 |url-access=registration |access-date=January 22, 2021 |website=www.medpagetoday.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Swinford |first=Steven |date=7 October 2020 |title=Lift coronavirus curbs and go for herd immunity, urges coalition of scientists |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/lift-coronavirus-curbs-and-go-for-herd-immunity-urges-coalition-of-scientists-3599v25n3 |work=[[The Times]] }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite news |last=Sample |first=Ian |date=6 October 2020 |title=Scientists call for Covid herd immunity strategy for young |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/06/scientists-call-for-herd-immunity-covid-strategy-for-young |work=The Guardian }}</ref> The World Health Organization, as well as numerous other academic and public-health bodies, stated that the strategy proposed by the declaration is dangerous, unethical, and lacks a sound scientific basis.<ref name="GuardianTedros">{{cite news|author=Staff and agencies in Geneva|date=12 October 2020|title=WHO chief says herd immunity approach to pandemic 'unethical'|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/12/who-chief-says-herd-immunity-approach-to-pandemic-unethical|access-date=October 12, 2020}}</ref><ref name="WHOTedros">{{cite web|url=https://www.who.int/dg/speeches/detail/who-director-general-s-opening-remarks-at-the-media-briefing-on-covid-19---12-october-2020|title=WHO Director-General's opening remarks at the media briefing on COVID-19 – 12 October 2020|date=12 October 2020|access-date=12 October 2020|publisher=World Health Organization}}</ref> The [[American Public Health Association]] and 13 other public-health groups in the United States said in a joint open letter that the Great Barrington Declaration "is not a strategy, it is a political statement" and said it was "selling false hope that will predictably backfire".<ref name="Zilbermints">{{Cite web|last=Zilbermints|first=Regina|date=2020-10-15|title=Dozens of public health groups, experts blast 'herd immunity' strategy backed by White House|url=https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/521159-dozens-of-public-health-groups-experts-blast-herd-immunity-strategy-backed|access-date=2021-01-14|website=TheHill|language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, she was an author at the Brownstone Institute, a new think tank founded by [[Jeffrey Tucker]] where senior roles were held by [[Martin Kulldorff]] and [[Jay Bhattacharya]], her co-authors on the Great Barrington Declaration.<ref>{{Cite web|last=D'Ambrosio|first=Amanda|date=2021-11-11|title=New Institute Has Ties to the Great Barrington Declaration|url=https://www.medpagetoday.com/special-reports/exclusives/95601 |access-date=2021-11-27|website=MedPage Today |language=en}}</ref>

==Works of fiction==
Gupta wrote her first works of fiction in Bengali. She was a translator of the poetry of [[Rabindranath Tagore]]. She has published several novels in English. In October 2012 her fifth novel, ''So Good in Black'', was longlisted for the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.sunetragupta.com/biography.asp|title = biography|publisher = Sunetra Gupta|access-date = 1 September 2013}}</ref> Her novels have been awarded the [[Sahitya Akademi Award]], the [[Southern Arts Federation|Southern Arts]] Literature Prize, shortlisted for the [[Vodafone Crossword Book Award|Crossword Award]], and longlisted for the [[Orange Prize]].<ref>{{cite news |date=20 March 2000 |title=Orange Prize longlist announced |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2000/mar/20/news |work=The Guardian }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gupta was married to the Irish vaccinologist [[Adrian V. S. Hill]] from 1994 to 2020. They have two daughters.<ref name="Who's Who"/><ref>{{cite news|last=Loder|first=Natasha|date=2000-06-22|title=Oxford scientist wins the battle for her reputation|newspaper=Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1344293/Oxford-scientist-wins-the-battle-for-her-reputation.html|access-date=2016-01-25}}</ref><ref name="divorce">{{Cite web|date=2020-06-08|title=Corrections and clarifications|url=http://www.theguardian.com/news/2020/jun/08/corrections-and-clarifications|access-date=2020-10-21|website=The Guardian|language=en|quote="An interview with Prof Sunetra Gupta said she was married to Adrian Hill, the director of Oxford's Jenner Institute. This is no longer the case"}}</ref> She has dismissed claims of having a [[Right-wing politics|right-wing]] perspective, claiming to be "more Left than [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]]".<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |last=Fishwick |first=Samuel |date=13 October 2020 |title='I've had emails calling me evil'... Meet the Covid scientists at war |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/coronavirus-scientists-at-war-a4569551.html |access-date=17 October 2020 |website=Evening Standard |language=en}}</ref>
